speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These areas are open to the public so that everyone can enjoy them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In some of the newer estates, beautiful sky gardens with gorgeous views are built to the delight of all.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is the hope of the Government that our people will be able to spend time with their families, loved ones, neighbours and friends in these pockets of nature in the midst of our public housing estates and build cohesive communities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Unfortunately, not all users of these painstakingly-built sky gardens take care of these spaces nor consider the well-being of residents who live in the blocks where the gardens are located.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Unlike beaches and public parks, the sky gardens are literally built onto the residents' blocks, where inconsiderate and irresponsible usage have a direct impact on the people living there.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents have been putting up with the inconvenience and nuisance caused by visitors to the sky gardens who behave in an inconsiderate manner.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: These troubles are especially pronounced during the weekends, eve of festive seasons and public holidays.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My residents are well aware that these are public gardens, but they are extremely inconvenienced by the chaos, noise and the rubbish that the crowds would bring.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There were occasions when the wait time for lifts is very long because many non-residents are using the lifts to visit the sky gardens and the carpark lots are also taken up.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents sometimes have to endure dirty lifts, overflowing dustbins, littering, illegal smoking and loud partying in common areas.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On weekends, visitors go to these gardens late at night too and their noise also disturb residents trying to sleep.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In the morning, the cleaners are confronted with cigarette butts and alcohol bottles that are carelessly littered all over the sky gardens.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My volunteers patrol the sky gardens at night after 10 pm to remind visitors to leave the sky gardens as residents need to have their rest.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, my volunteers have been doing this for over two years.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Expecting them to patrol these gardens daily is not only time-consuming but unsustainable.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The issues are no longer happening on a daily basis with the reopening of borders and lifting of restrictions on the gathering of people, but such problems are still observed during weekends and on festive occasions.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Over the last few years, we have tried so many measures to minimise the disamenities, together with HDB, Town Council, Residents' Committees, the National Environment Agency (NEA) and other Government agencies.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope we can move on and try new measures.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My residents and I are mindful that these are public spaces.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But public access is not a licence to abuse the space, or behave inconsiderately and irresponsibly.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The current state of affairs is hardly building cohesive communities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Residents are stressed by the many strangers loitering around their dwelling units and creating disamenities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In contrast, the situation at another popular HDB rooftop terrace at Pinnacle @ Duxton is much more orderly.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: During the earlier days of the COVID-19 pandemic, the Pinnacle @ Duxton rooftop was closed to visitors.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I earnestly appeal for similar preventive measures to ensure the orderly management of public access to all other HDB sky gardens all over Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They just want measures to enable them to live normally and peacefully, which most HDB residents do everywhere.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The current system is not allowing this, and we have to implement measures to ensure security and crowd control to reduce disamenities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: HDB sky gardens are here to stay, and we will expect to see more of such beautiful features in future developments.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But the need to share these public spaces in a responsible manner is equally important as well.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope we can all work together towards a more sustainable set of solutions together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB estates are designed to be open and inclusive and to foster community bonding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In line with this philosophy, HDB estates are not gated and remain accessible not just to residents but also members of the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also design community gardens, void decks and other community spaces in our estates to foster interactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such spaces are, as a matter of policy, kept open and accessible to all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is one of the distinctive differences between public and private housing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In the past decade, sky gardens have been introduced to newer estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They function as a refuge floor for fire protection in residential blocks above 40 storeys and provide skyrise greenery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Sky gardens may include additional facilities, such as fitness corners and sheltered seating areas for people to exercise together, chit chat or gather as a community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: While they are located above ground, they are, in essence, similar to other common spaces in public housing estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I understand the Member's concerns about how some members of the public have been treating the sky gardens as an attraction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: From a policy perspective, HDB cannot treat sky gardens as exclusive enclosed spaces.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: At the same time, we acknowledge that sky gardens are not identical in nature to the ground-level open parks and green spaces that we see in many HDB estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Because of their elevation and the views that they command, sky gardens might attract visitors who would not go out of their way to visit ground-level HDB parks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: And because sky gardens can only be accessed via lifts, visitors will end up sharing these lifts with residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is different from ground-level HDB parks that often have multiple points of access.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Thus, if the sky gardens attract an unusual volume of visitors during peak times, even residents who do not use the sky gardens regularly might feel inconvenienced by crowding in lifts or at the lift lobbies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: What we are able to do is to assist the Town Councils and the local grassroots in signalling to visitors that sky gardens, while open in nature, are residential amenities and not domestic tourist attractions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Visitors should not forget that residents live very near the sky gardens, and/or behave in an inconsiderate and irresponsible manner, such as making loud noises, smoking or littering.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Therefore, HDB has been actively working with Town Councils and various Government agencies to implement measures targeted at addressing these disamenities that bring inconvenience and stress to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: In 2016, a task force was established to manage crowds at the respective sky gardens on the eve of festivities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB is a member of this task force, focused at SkyVille and SkyTerrace, along with the Residents' Committee, Tanjong Pagar Town Council, Singapore Police Force (SPF), as well as NEA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is on top of increased SPF patrols and NEA's own patrols targeted at smoking and littering offences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: More signages and CCTV cameras were installed as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB had also conducted special joint operations with the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), NEA and Dawson Residents' Committee, to address feedback on the non-compliance of COVID-19 safe management measures (SMMs) at the sky gardens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: From September to November 2021, the team issued advisories to members of the public on the proper wearing of masks, observing safe distancing and keeping to group size limits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For more serious breaches, HDB issued Notices of Composition (NOC) to offenders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Overall, members of the public complied with the SMMs after receiving the advisories.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Apart from the isolated incidents, the sky gardens were relatively quiet, with no breaches of group size limits and no serious or deliberate non-compliance of SMMs observed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: On New Year's Eve 2021, the sky gardens at SkyVille were closed from 10 pm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The task force observed minimal crowds and SMMs were not breached.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Groups readily dispersed and left the premises upon being advised by the task force.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Notices have been placed around the sky gardens with the help of Tanjong Pagar Town Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Since New Year's Eve 2020, HDB's on-site inspections have shown that the number of visitors to the sky gardens has declined significantly and large gatherings are uncommon, with users generally cleaning up after themselves and behaving in an orderly manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Thus far, HDB has not received any recent feedback from residents pertaining to disamenities on sky gardens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Even though the situation on the ground appears to have stabilised, we agree with the need for constant surveillance and vigilance, through the use of signages and CCTV cameras to warn visitors and deter errant behaviour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Similar to the sky garden at SkyVille, all skyrise gardens and terraces in other HDB projects remain open to all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Member raised the case of Pinnacle @ Duxton, where access to its 50th storey sky bridge is chargeable and gated for non-residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It was assessed at the project design stage then, that there was a need to limit access to its sky bridges in view of various factors, such as the development's central location, its iconic status as the tallest HDB residential building in Singapore, as well as the novelty of the panoramic city views on offer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: During my visit to one of these sky gardens, I was heartened to hear Ms Pereira explain that her residents are not asking for or expecting zero visitors to the sky gardens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: What they want is for the disamenities to be managed and for daily living not to be disrupted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is a reasonable expectation and, in fact, similar to resident expectations of how ground-level HDB parks are managed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ground-level HDB parks might also attract littering, loitering or noisy congregations from time to time, but these issues are, by and large, addressable through the advice and action on the part of agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Creating a quality living environment requires everyone to play their part.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I hope that as a society, we can be considerate and kind to one another, and make our HDB estates an icon of gracious, inclusive and harmonious living.

speaker: Mdm Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Pereira, as we have some time, do you want to seek any clarification on the Senior Minister of State's reply?
